area_summary:
The settings UIs are small and mostly sound, and app.js already keeps server data out of innerHTML. The biggest cost is in the CSS. Electron runs with hardware acceleration disabled (main.js:18), so it composites in software. In that mode the infinite status pulses force a full recomposition every frame: the sticky header's backdrop blur, a full-viewport overlay-blend grain layer, and an empty blurred body::before (its gradient syntax is invalid, so it never draws anything). I measured about 55-60% of one core while the window shows 'connecting' or 'awaiting_link', using headless Chrome 153 with --disable-gpu as a stand-in. Three of these effects make no visible difference (pixel-checked) and the fourth can be limited to the scrolled state, which brings the cost to about 5-7%. Next in importance:
- **Security:** a malicious or compromised bot, or a ws:// man-in-the-middle, can inject markup through innerHTML in settings.js and navigate the settings window to a remote page that then gets the preload API. Verified in Chrome with the real CSP.
- **Rendering cost:** every history row creates a new date formatter, which makes each history render about 15x slower than needed. This matters most on Android, where every Hub change, including during an APK download or while the app is in the background, rebuilds the whole state and DOM.
- **Hidden window:** the Windows settings window is only hidden on close, so it keeps polling every 30 and 60 seconds.
- **Robustness:** neither Android WebView handles onRenderProcessGone, so a renderer crash kills the whole process, including the foreground service.
- **Small UI bugs:** the opacity slider fill is wrong when the window opens, the blocked-users list stays visible after disconnecting, and the display picker goes stale or blank.

The repo was not modified. The test harness, screenshots and benchmarks are under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-memedrop/065ca17e-4939-5472-b348-276c03e80469/scratchpad/audit-scratch/settings-ui/.

findings.title: Status pulses force per-frame blur and blend recomposition (about 55-60% of a core in software compositing)
findings.evidence: styles.css:171-172 and :667 run an infinite `pulse` on the pill dot (connecting/awaiting) and on the status icon. The dot sits inside `.pill` (backdrop-filter blur(6px), l.161), which sits inside the sticky `.topbar` (blur(14px), l.69). Underneath are a fixed full-viewport `.grain` with mix-blend-mode overlay (l.53-61) and `body::before` with filter blur(50px) (l.40-51). Its background is invalid (no comma after each rgba() stop, so getComputedStyle gives background-image 'none'), yet it still gets a 1100x1383 composited layer (CDP LayerTree). main.js:18 disables hardware acceleration. Measured with headless Chrome 153 --disable-gpu, DSF 1.5, CPU summed over all processes: awaiting 61%, connecting 54% of one core. Without grain, pill blur and ::before: 46%. Also without the topbar blur: 5-7%. Linked state (no animation): 1.3%.
findings.behavior_change: none (measured pixel diffs at most 4/255; up to 14/255 on about 40 anti-aliased pill-border pixels at 2.6x)
findings.cross_component: settings.html:14 and android assets/app.html:42 (grain div). Step 4 needs settings.js and app.js changed together because styles.css is shared.
findings.risk: Low. The CPU figures come from headless Chrome as a stand-in for Electron 33 software compositing, so absolute values will differ, but the ranking (topbar blur > grain > the rest) should hold. Android composites on the GPU, so the gain is smaller there but goes the same way.
findings.value: While the window shows connecting or awaiting (pairing, bot reconnects), CPU drops from about 55-60% to about 5-7% of a core. Scrolling also gets cheaper, and phones have fewer layers and offscreen passes per frame.

findings.title: Server strings (pairing code, guild and user IDs) go through innerHTML and can navigate the settings window
findings.evidence: settings.js:105 does `serversTip.innerHTML = `.../link ${code}...`` with code = raw msg.code (main.js:440). :140 `ID ${g.id}` and :183 `ID ${b.id}` (links sent by the server) also go into innerHTML. The CSP stops scripts but not markup. Verified in Chrome with the real CSP: a code, guild id or blocked-user id of `` navigated the page to that remote URL, through all 3 sinks. In Electron the preload runs on every navigation, so the remote page gets window.memedrop inside the trusted window: settings:set stores any key (main.js:629), plus openExternal, replay, etc. It could also show a phishing page there. This needs a malicious or compromised bot, or a ws:// MITM (ws:// is accepted).
findings.behavior_change: none for legitimate data (same text and markup)
findings.risk: None. Output is identical for numeric codes and Discord snowflake IDs.
findings.value: Closes a path from HTML injection to navigating the privileged window, which would expose the IPC bridge to a remote page.

findings.title: History rendering creates a new date formatter for every row (about 15x slower than needed)
findings.evidence: settings.js:257,266,335 and app.js:251,259,307 call toLocaleDateString/toLocaleTimeString('fr-FR', {...}) for each history row. With explicit options, V8 builds a new ICU formatter on every call. Measured in Chrome 153: 0.21 ms per call, versus 0.003 ms with a reused Intl.DateTimeFormat. settings.js renderHistory (20 rows): 6.4 ms, down to 0.41 ms. One Android push (onNativeState): 6.8 ms JS, or 9.6 ms with layout, down to 0.45 ms (2.0 ms with layout), on a desktop core. The text output is identical (checked). On Android this runs on every push (twice a second during an APK download, on each setting commit, each drop, every 30 s). On Windows it runs on each drop and every 60 s, even while the window is hidden.
findings.behavior_change: none (identical strings: same locale and options)
findings.risk: Very low. Intl.DateTimeFormat exists on every target (Electron 33, WebView 80 and later).
findings.value: History renders about 15x faster. This is most of the cost of each Android state push, which is janky on low-end phones (estimated 40-60 ms per push on cores 5-8x slower).

findings.title: Android settings rebuild the full state and DOM on every Hub change, even in background
findings.evidence: app.js:404-409 calls the synchronous MD.getState() and then render() on every push, rebuilding the server list, blocked list and 20-row history. It also runs every 30 s (l.413). MainActivity.kt:52 adds the Hub listener in onCreate and l.64 removes it only in onDestroy, so pushes continue while the activity is stopped. Hub.changed() fires on each connection transition (2 per reconnect attempt while offline), each drop, each setting commit (MainActivity.kt:121), and every 500 ms during an APK download, even when progress has not changed or the download is paused (Updater.kt:95-120). Each time, stateJson() (MainActivity.kt:79-101) parses about 12 KB of history and the settings twice, and makes 2 binder calls (canDrawOverlays, isIgnoringBatteryOptimizations).
findings.cross_component: MainActivity.kt (listener lifecycle, perm cache) and Updater.kt poll (optional)
findings.risk: Low. The guard relies on the WebView reporting document.hidden once the activity is stopped (AwContents hides its WebContents when the window becomes invisible; about 80% sure). If it does not, the guard never triggers and nothing regresses. The onStart/onStop change gives the same result either way.
findings.value: No getState, JSON or DOM work while the app is in background. The process runs around the clock because of the foreground service. Also fewer bridge round-trips and re-renders during downloads and reconnect loops.

findings.title: A WebView renderer crash kills the whole app, including the foreground service
findings.evidence: Neither the settings WebViewClient (MainActivity.kt:39-48) nor the overlay's (OverlayController.kt:96-103) overrides onRenderProcessGone. Since API 26 the default returns false, and the WebViewClient docs say the app 'will crash if render process crashed, or be killed if render process was killed by the system'. Android WebView uses one renderer process per app. So if that renderer runs out of memory or crashes while a drop plays (a big GIF or video on a low-RAM phone), MemeDropService dies too whenever an unhandled WebView exists, for example the settings activity kept alive in background. This follows from the API contract; I did not reproduce it.
findings.proposed_change:
MainActivity, in the client object at l.39:
```kotlin
override fun onRenderProcessGone(view: WebView, detail: RenderProcessGoneDetail): Boolean {
    // Renderer (partagé avec l'overlay) perdu : on recrée l'écran plutôt que de laisser Android tuer le process (et le service)
    webDead = true
    recreate()
    return true
}
```
Add `private var webDead = false`, and in pushState() use `if (::web.isInitialized && !webDead)`, because the dead WebView must not be used again.
OverlayController's client: `override fun onRenderProcessGone(view: WebView, detail: RenderProcessGoneDetail): Boolean { Hub.main.post { destroy() }; return true }`. The next drop recreates the WebView.
findings.behavior_change: bugfix: a renderer crash no longer kills the foreground service
findings.cross_component: OverlayController.kt:96 (both clients must handle it; one unhandled client is enough to kill the process)
findings.risk: Low. API 26+, and minSdk is 26. onDestroy still calls web.destroy() on the dead view, which is allowed.
findings.value: The 24/7 service survives WebView renderer crashes and out-of-memory kills.

findings.title: Opacity slider fill is drawn in the wrong place when the window opens
findings.evidence: settings.js:631 sets `opEl.style.setProperty('--value', `${opEl.value}%`)`, but #opacity has min=20 and max=100 (settings.html:300). bindRange (l.557) uses the correct `(v-min)*100/(max-min)`. Verified: with opacity 0.2 the fill covers 20% of the track while the thumb is at 0% ('--value' is '20%' at open, '0%' after the first input event), and the screenshot shows the blue fill running past the thumb. Lines 621, 626, 636 and 641 repeat the formula with hard-coded bounds.
findings.behavior_change: bugfix: the opacity fill matches the thumb when the window opens (other sliders unchanged)
findings.value: Fixes a visible glitch and removes 5 duplicated formulas.

findings.title: Blocked-users card stays visible, with dead buttons, after disconnect, pause or unlink
findings.evidence: On every state, applyConnState (settings.js:389-395) hides the pairing, linked, servers and status cards, but not blockedCard. renderBlockedPanel only runs in the 'linked' case (l.415). Verified: after a 'disconnected' or 'paused' push the 'Utilisateurs bloqués' card stays visible. Clicking 'débloquer' calls unblockUser, and main's wsSend() returns false when there is no socket (main.js:386-389, 674-675), so nothing happens and there is no feedback. After 'unlinked' the previous account's list stays on screen. Android hides it when not linked (app.js:198-200).
findings.proposed_change: In the reset block of applyConnState (after l.395), add `blockedCard.classList.add('hidden');`. renderBlockedPanel() shows it again in the 'linked' case.
findings.behavior_change: bugfix: the blocked list is hidden when not linked, as on Android
findings.value: Removes stale data and buttons that silently do nothing.

findings.title: Hidden settings window keeps polling every 30/60 s and keeps a stale display list
findings.evidence: On close the window is hidden, not destroyed (main.js:251-256), and main.js:19 disables background timer throttling. So after the first open, two intervals run around the clock. `setInterval(refreshQuietHours, 30_000)` (l.234) sends an IPC whose handler calls store.get, which in conf 10.2 re-reads and parses config.json. `setInterval(() => renderHistory(historyEntries), 60_000)` (l.366) rebuilds the full history DOM (6.4 ms measured). Separately, listDisplays() runs only once, in init (l.654). A monitor plugged in later never appears until restart. If the stored overlayDisplayId no longer exists, the select is blank (verified: selectedIndex -1), while main actually uses the primary display (main.js:134-142).
findings.behavior_change: bugfix: the display list refreshes when the window is reopened, and a missing monitor shows 'Écran principal (auto)' (what main actually uses) instead of a blank select
findings.risk: Low. Electron reports document.hidden after win.hide() or minimize for windows with backgroundThrottling on, which is the default for this window.
findings.value: No work while hidden (about 4300 timer wake-ups per day today) and a correct display picker.

findings.title: Google Fonts loaded from the network block first paint and contact Google on every open
findings.evidence: settings.html:8-10 and app.html:7-9 preconnect to fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com, then load the font CSS as a parser-inserted <link> in <head>. That blocks rendering and every script after it. Measured with the CSS delayed by 5 s (a local slow server standing in for a slow or captive network): first paint at 5240 ms, settings.js ran at 5247 ms, so the window stays blank and unusable. The preconnects open 2 TLS connections to Google on every page load (each MainActivity creation on Android), even when the CSS is cached. Users' IP and user agent go to Google (a GDPR concern, cf. LG München 2022), and an offline first run falls back to system fonts.
findings.proposed_change:
Self-host the fonts:
- Put woff2 latin subsets in overlay/src/fonts/: Bricolage Grotesque (variable, 500-800), JetBrains Mono (variable, 500-700), Instrument Serif italic. They are OFL-licensed, about 100-150 KB total.
- Declare each in styles.css, e.g. `@font-face { font-family: 'Bricolage Grotesque'; src: url('fonts/bricolage.woff2') format('woff2'); font-weight: 500 800; font-display: swap; }`.
- Delete settings.html:8-10 and app.html:7-9.
- In the settings.html CSP, use `font-src 'self'` and drop https://fonts.googleapis.com from style-src.
- Add "fonts/**" to the include in syncWebAssets (android/app/build.gradle.kts:12).
Note: fonts.googleapis.com returns 403 through this sandbox's proxy, so the owner has to fetch the files.
findings.behavior_change: none once the fonts are bundled (same typefaces); offline and first runs get the real fonts
findings.risk: Low. Adds about 150 KB per package, and the OFL license text must ship with the fonts. It cannot be done here without the font files.
findings.value: No render-blocking network request, no third-party request on every open, and the same look offline.

findings.title: Screen-reader gaps: Android tabs expose no state, unlabeled images, identical switch names
findings.evidence: app.html:62-67: the tab buttons have no role or aria-selected, and showTab (app.js:21) only toggles a CSS class, so TalkBack cannot tell which tab is active (settings.js:61 does set aria-selected). app.js:193 (guild icons) and :311 (20 history avatars) create without alt, so each is read as an unlabeled image (settings.js sets alt=''). settings.js:144-148: the per-server switches have no label, only the title 'Cliquer pour désactiver ce serveur' when checked, so every switch gets the same name and none includes the server's name. In settings.html, the panels behind the role="tab" buttons lack role="tabpanel".
findings.proposed_change:
- app.html:62: `<nav class="tabs" role="tablist">`, and `role="tab"` on the 4 buttons.
- app.js:21: `tabs.forEach(t => { const on = t.dataset.tab === name; t.classList.toggle('active', on); t.setAttribute('aria-selected', String(on)); });`.
- app.js:193 `pic.alt = '';` and :311 `img.alt = '';`.
- settings.js after l.148: `sw.setAttribute('aria-label', `Recevoir les drops de ${g.name || 'ce serveur'}`);`.
- Add `role="tabpanel"` to the .tab-panel divs in both HTML files.
findings.behavior_change: none visually; screen readers get correct names and states
findings.value: Basic accessibility fixes at no cost.
